## Inspiration guide

The most complete, practical reference I found is IGN’s **[All Recipes and Cookbook](https://www.ign.com/wikis/the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild/All_Recipes_and_Cookbook)**. It has **118 recipe rows** and is organized by vegetarian, seafood, meat, surf-and-turf, desserts, monster foods, and snacks. It also lists the in-game ingredient combinations, so it is excellent for naming/display inspiration.

For your dessert table, its most useful in-game names are:

- **Fruitcake** — wildberry or apple, another fruit, cane sugar, Tabantha wheat  
- **Fruit Pie**
- **Honeyed Fruits**
- **Egg Tart**
- **Wildberry Crepe**
- **Monster Cake**
- **Fried Bananas**

## Best inexpensive dessert plan

### Main: “Chilly Fruitcake” — pineapple Dole-Whip-style cups
This gives the tropical look but uses an actual BOTW dessert name. Add a tiny menu subtitle like: *“Frozen pineapple cream, from the Faron frontier.”*

**For about 4 generous cups:**
- 1 10-oz bag frozen pineapple chunks
- 1 pint vanilla ice cream
- 1 6-oz can pineapple juice
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice, optional but helpful

**Method**
1. Blend the juice, lemon juice, ice cream, and frozen pineapple until smooth.
2. Freeze in a loaf pan about 45 minutes, until scoopable/pipeable.
3. Scoop into small clear cups. If you have a piping bag and star tip, pipe a swirl; otherwise, a spooned mound still looks good.
4. Optional cheap garnish: one maraschino cherry, paper cocktail pick, or a small sprinkle of crushed graham crackers.

The recipe source I read specifies those amounts, about **5 minutes of prep**, and roughly **45 minutes** to get the soft-serve texture. It says the batch yields **4 cups**. [Source: Simply Recipes](https://www.simplyrecipes.com/copycat-disney-dole-whip-recipe-12128437)

**Cheap shortcut:** Skip fresh-pineapple garnish, fancy cups, and piping tools. Use small paper cups/bowls and call it “Chilly Fruitcake.” Make it close to serving time; it gets firmer if held frozen much longer.

### Chocolate backup: “Monster Cake”
Make the easiest possible version: a **boxed chocolate cake** in a 9×13 pan or cupcakes, with chocolate frosting.

To make it Zelda-ish without expensive decorating:
- Frost it dark brown/black.
- Sprinkle with crushed chocolate cookies or chocolate sprinkles.
- Add 2–3 candy eyes per serving, or pipe simple white “eyes.”
- Put a funny caveat on the menu: **“Monster Cake — surprisingly edible.”**

That references the game’s Monster Cake while avoiding anything complicated. The IGN guide lists Monster Cake as a dessert/monster-food item, so the label will land even if your recipe is simply chocolate cake.

**If serving a crowd:** Do the Dole-style cups as the featured limited item and a sheet-pan Monster Cake as the reliable, room-temperature backup. It is cheaper and less stressful than making two frozen desserts.

## Simple sign/menu with an X-Carve

### Lowest-effort design
Use a small scrap of plywood, MDF, or pine—something around **8×12 in.** is plenty. In Easel:
1. Create a rectangle matching the board.
2. Add only two large lines of text:
   ```
   HYRULE DESSERTS
   Chilly Fruitcake
   Monster Cake
   ```
3. Add a simple **Triforce-inspired three-triangle icon** or a small leaf/rupee-like diamond—not a detailed graphic.
4. Use a shallow **fill carve** for text/icons rather than a deep 3D carve.
5. Paint the face dark green, brown, or black first; carve afterward to expose pale wood. This is much easier than trying to paint inside letters.
6. Sand lightly and seal only if needed.

For a fast carve, keep letters bold and at least roughly ¾–1 inch tall, avoid skinny script fonts and tiny detail, and do one shallow pass. Easel’s official site says you can open gallery projects, change the words, wood, and size, then send them to the machine: [Easel](https://easel.inventables.com/). The X-Carve instructions page also directs users to finish initial carving setup in Easel: [X-Carve instructions](https://x-carve-instructions.inventables.com/1000mm/step11/).

**Even cheaper/faster alternative:** Carve only **“HYRULE DESSERTS”** and use a paper menu card beneath it for the two dessert descriptions. That avoids recarving if the menu changes.

## Mirror the iPhone for inspiration

### If you have an Apple TV, AirPlay-capable TV, or compatible Mac
1. Put the iPhone and receiving device on the **same Wi‑Fi**.
2. On iPhone X or later, swipe down from the **upper-right corner** to open Control Center.
3. Tap **Screen Mirroring**.
4. Choose the TV or Mac.
5. Enter the passcode shown on that screen, if prompted.

To stop: Control Center → Screen Mirroring → **Stop Mirroring**.

That is Apple’s current procedure: [Apple Support: AirPlay / Screen Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102661).

**Practical event tip:** Open the recipe/inspiration page first, turn on Do Not Disturb, and keep the phone plugged in. If Wi‑Fi is unreliable, a wired HDMI adapter appropriate for your iPhone plus an HDMI cable is the more dependable fallback—but AirPlay is the free option if the equipment is already there.

## Restore the iPad’s tiny floating keyboard

When the small floating keyboard is visible, place two fingers on it and **spread them apart**—a pinch-open gesture. Apple states that this returns it to the full-size keyboard.

You can also drag the small keyboard downward, but **pinch open** is the direct fix. [Apple iPad keyboard guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/type-with-the-onscreen-keyboard-ipad997da459/ipados)

## Ready-to-copy menu wording

```text
HYRULE DESSERTS

CHILLY FRUITCAKE
Frozen pineapple cream
Faron-style refreshment

MONSTER CAKE
Dark chocolate cake
Surprisingly edible
```

This keeps the theme recognizable, the ingredients ordinary, the sign quick to carve, and the setup manageable.
